transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I, um, I hope I'm giving you the right information here, and I'm sure it's probably nothing too serious. I just... well, I've been a little embarrassed lately at work. 

I'm a jeweler, you see, and I came in because when people ask me a really simple question—like, oh, just asking when a ring repair will be ready—I try to answer, but my words just sort of get away from me. My answer will start out fine, but then it goes from the shop invoices, and then somehow I'm talking about garden soil, and then my mortgage papers... 

I know it sounds a bit silly, and I'm probably just making a mountain out of a molehill, but I can see the customers looking at me and I know they're completely losing me. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to know.
Have you ever felt that your thoughts are being put into your mind by someone else, or that your thoughts are being taken out or broadcasted to others?

Oh, goodness, no. No, I haven't ever felt anything like that. My thoughts are definitely my own... they just, well, they just get a bit tangled up on their way out of my mouth sometimes. 

I hope it's okay that I don't have that happening—I mean, I really don't want to waste your time if you're looking for something more serious. But no, nobody is putting thoughts in my head or broadcasting them or anything like that. Does that make sense? Am I answering your question the right way?
Have you ever believed something very strongly that others around you didn't seem to understand or agree with, even though you felt certain it was true?

Well, um... I guess there is one thing. I really hope it doesn't sound too strange, and I'm sure it's probably just me being a little oversensitive. I don't want you to think I'm paranoid or anything like that. 

But lately, I've just been... well, I've gotten quite convinced that some of the customers coming into the shop aren't actually there to buy jewelry. I know it sounds odd, but I really feel like they're coming in just to check up on me, to see if I'm going to miss payments on the shop. They just ask so many questions about the new showroom we put in, and it feels very... pointed. 

My husband tells me they're just being friendly and making conversation, and I'm sure he's probably right. I know I shouldn't think that way. I just... I can't shake the feeling that they're checking up on my finances. Is that the kind of thing you meant? I hope I'm not sounding too foolish.

Can you tell me more about why you believe the customers are checking up on your finances? Have you noticed any specific behaviors or comments from them that support this belief, or is it more of a feeling you get?

Well, um... I guess it's mostly a feeling, but it just seems like they linger too long by the new display cases, you know? And they ask things like, "Oh, this must have been quite an investment," or "Business must be doing well to afford this." 

I know, I know, my husband says they're just being polite and admiring the work we've done. And I really, really want to believe him. I know I probably shouldn't be reading so much into it. But it just... it feels so specific. Like they're trying to figure out if we overextended ourselves and if we're going to lose the shop. 

I'm sorry, I know it sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud. I don't want you to think I'm making things up or being overly suspicious. I just can't seem to shake that feeling when they start asking about the showroom. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining it alright for you.
Have you been able to let go of that belief, even a little, when your husband or others have reassured you that the customers are just being friendly?

Well, I... I try to. I really do try to listen to him. When he says they're just being friendly, I always nod and agree, because I know he's trying to help, and I don't want to cause any trouble or make him worry. 

But... if I'm being completely honest—and I hope it's okay to say this—I just haven't been able to let it go. Even after he reassures me, I'm still just so convinced they're coming in to check if I'll miss payments. I know it sounds odd, and I really wish I could just brush it off like he does. I'm sorry, I know I'm probably being difficult about this. I just can't seem to stop believing it, no matter how much he tells me they're just being nice. Is it bad that I can't let it go? I'm really trying, I promise.

Even though your husband has reassured you that the customers are just being friendly and admiring the showroom, do you still believe, without any doubt, that they are actually checking up on your finances?

Oh... I really hate to admit this, because I know how stubborn it makes me sound. And I really want to be agreeable and just tell you that I'm doubting it now. But... yes. If I'm being completely honest, I am still just absolutely convinced that they are coming in to check whether I'll miss payments. 

Even after my husband says they're only being friendly... I just keep going back to how they ask way too many questions about the new showroom. It just feels so real to me, and I can't find any doubt in my mind about it, no matter how hard I try. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's probably not the right answer, and I really don't want to seem like I'm just ignoring my husband's help. Am I sounding totally unreasonable to you? I really hope you don't think badly of me for it.
Can you tell me if you have any other beliefs that others around you don't share and that you feel completely certain about, even when they can't see it the same way you do?

Oh, um... well... I don't think so? I really don't want to seem like I have all these... strange ideas. I try very hard to stay grounded, I really do. 

I think it's just that one thing, really. Just the... the feeling about the customers checking up on the payments because of the new showroom. That's the only thing that I just can't seem to see eye-to-eye with my husband on, no matter how much he tells me they're just being nice. 

I don't have any other thoughts like that, I promise. I try to be very agreeable with everyone else about everything else. I hope that's okay? I really don't want to be a difficult case for you.
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs that something was happening or true, even when others couldn’t see it the same way you did?

Um... no, really, I haven't. I know I just said this, and I'm so sorry if I'm not explaining myself well enough or if I misunderstood you... but it truly is just that one situation with the customers and the showroom. 

I've never had anything else like that happen where I... where I saw things so differently from everyone else. I always try to be very agreeable and reasonable in my life. I really do. I hope it's okay that I don't have anything else to tell you about that? I promise I'm not trying to hide anything from you, I just... I really want to make sure I'm giving you the right answers. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had any experiences where you believed something was real or happening to you that others around you didn’t seem to notice or agree with—even small things?

Oh... um... well, I guess... if you mean really small things, maybe? I really hesitate to bring this up because I don't want you to think I'm losing my mind or anything like that. I'm usually very practical, being a jeweler, you know? You have to be.

But sometimes... just when the shop is completely quiet, I'll... I'll think I hear a woman muttering my name. It sounds like it's coming from the polishing room. And sometimes I'll smell burning metal, even when I know for an absolute fact that all the torches are turned off. 

It's probably just stress, right? Or just my imagination playing tricks on me because I'm tired. But it feels real enough in the moment that I actually get up and go check the back room, just to be safe. 

I hope that doesn't sound too strange? It's really nothing major, I promise. Just little things like that. Does... does that sound like the kind of thing you were asking about? I really want to be helpful.

When you hear the woman muttering your name or smell burning metal, are there any actual people around or any source of those smells, or does it happen when you're completely alone and there's nothing causing those things?

Um... no, there's no one else there. It's just me. I mean, my husband is usually out front, but the polishing room is completely empty when it happens. 

And the torches... I always double-check them before I close up the back, so I know they're off. But I still smell it, and I still hear her. Just... muttering my name. It feels so real that I have to go look, just to make absolutely sure. 

I know it sounds silly, checking an empty room. I'm sorry, I probably shouldn't even have mentioned it. It's just my mind playing tricks on me because I'm so tired, right? I really try not to let it bother me too much. I hope it's okay that I brought it up... I just want to give you the right answers.

When you hear the woman muttering your name or smell burning metal, is there ever any actual person present or any physical source for the smell, or does it happen even when you’re completely alone and nothing is causing those sensations?

Um... well, like I said, it's... it's usually just me. I mean, it happens when the shop is completely quiet, you know? Just me in the back. There's definitely no woman in the polishing room, and I know for a fact the torches are off because I'm very careful about safety. 

So, no... there's no actual person there, and no real fire or anything. It's just... it just feels so real in that moment that I have to go check. I'm sorry to repeat myself, I just want to make sure I'm answering your question properly. Is that... is that what you needed to know? I really hope I'm not making too big a deal out of this, it's probably just stress from work.

Are there any times when you hear the woman muttering your name or smell burning metal, but you’re absolutely certain there’s no actual source for those experiences, like someone nearby speaking or the torch being on?

Oh, um... yes. I'm so sorry, I must not be explaining myself very well, and I really don't want to frustrate you. But yes, I am absolutely certain. 

When the shop gets quiet and I hear the woman muttering my name from the polishing room, or I catch that smell of burning metal... I know for a fact the torches are off and the room is empty. I'm positive there's no actual source. It's just... well, it just feels real enough to me in that split second that I still get up and go check anyway. Just to be completely safe. 

Am I... am I making sense now? I really hope I'm answering this right for you. It's honestly just a silly little quirk, nothing you need to worry about.

Do these experiences of hearing your name or smelling burning metal happen even when you're not expecting them or looking for them — like, do they come on suddenly without any trigger, or only when you're especially stressed or tired?

Um, well... I'm never really looking for it, if that makes sense. It does just sort of happen out of nowhere. Like I mentioned, the shop will just be perfectly quiet, and then suddenly I'll hear her muttering my name, or get that burning metal smell when the torches are completely off. It just catches me off guard, and it always feels real enough that I have to go check. 

But... I really do try to tell myself it's just because I'm tired or stressed out from work. That's probably when it happens the most, I think. That's pretty normal for someone working long hours, right? Your mind just sort of plays tricks on you when you're exhausted. I hope I'm being helpful... I really want to make sure I'm giving you what you need. Does that answer your question okay?
Do these experiences of hearing your name or smelling burning metal ever happen when you’re not stressed or tired, like during a calm or relaxed moment?

Um... well, honestly... I guess sometimes it does happen when things are pretty calm. Like, if I'm just sitting in the back and the shop is quiet, and I'm not feeling particularly overwhelmed or anything... I'll still hear her muttering my name from the polishing room. Or I'll get that sudden smell of burning metal, even when I know the torches are off. 

It still feels real enough that I go check, just to be absolutely sure. But... I mean, even when I'm relaxed, maybe my brain is just so used to the sounds and smells of the shop that it just sort of... fills in the blanks? I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm giving you all the wrong answers. Is it... is it bad that it happens when I'm calm, too? I really hope I'm not making things too complicated for you.

When you hear the woman muttering your name or smell burning metal, do these experiences feel like they are happening in real time, as if someone is actually speaking or something is actually burning, even though you know there’s no real source?

Yes, yes, exactly. Um, it really does feel like it's happening right then and there. That's why I always end up getting up from my bench to go check the polishing room, even when I know I'm alone in the shop and the torches are definitely off. 

It's just... it's so vivid in that exact second. I'll hear her muttering, or I'll catch that sharp smell of the metal, and my first instinct is just, 'Oh, someone's back there,' or 'I left a torch on.' It's only after I look and see that it's empty that I realize there wasn't anything there. 

I'm sorry, I know I keep repeating myself about checking the room. I just want to make sure I'm explaining it the way you need me to. Does that make sense? I'm not sounding too... crazy, am I? I promise I know it's not really happening once I look.
